name: Querandi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct, unclassifiable (Uruguay/Argentina); Glottolog lists no descriptive references; only scant colonial word records exist.

sources.citation: Gómez, Guillermo Luciano; Gorbalán, Carla Hebe; Viegas Barros, José Pedro; Domínguez, Luisa; De Mauro, Sofía; Malvestitti, Marisa. 2023. Ejhu Taluhet bajiná. Caminos colaborativos para la recuperación de la lengua querandí het. Cuadernos de Literatura 21, e2108, 17 pp. doi:10.30972/clt.0216893
sources.note: Gives a tentative consonant inventory (Tabla 6) and five vowels (Tabla 7) inferred from 16th-17th-c. proper names; nothing on where stress falls. Only remark on accent (p. 10): written sources vary 'en la acentuación: Tancaolquepen / Tancaolquepén (nombre de jefe querandí)'. Also notes the language is written today with the Spanish alphabet and that a consultant calls it 'una lengua nasal, pero no gutural'.
sources.venue: Caminos colaborativos para la recuperación de la lengua querandí het

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record quer1237 (Hammarström et al.), with reference records 111730 (Casamiquela 1969) and 27715 (Outes 1897)
sources.note: No descriptive references in the language page; the JSON 'meds' field names Casamiquela 1969 (type 'phonology or text collection', p. 55; ref page says 'A few words attributable to Querandí from Thevet') and Outes 1897 ('a wordlist or less'). Classification: Unclassifiable; AES extinct.

Nothing on stress. Report the whole attested corpus: two phrases in Thevet, Cosmographie universelle (1575) - 'Assaganoup o zoba', 'Caudy caudy vvuahiph gomálat' - plus zobá 'moon', afia 'bow' in Loukotka 1968; Bárcena's 16th-c. 'Arte y vocabulario' is lost; possible link to Gününa Küne (Viegas Barros).

sources.citation: Domínguez, Luisa. 2022. Entre «papeles viejos»: Félix F. Outes y la arqueología documental sobre lenguas indígenas en la Argentina de entresiglos. Lingüística y Literatura 43(81): 176-191.
sources.note: Historiography of the Querandí documentary record; would confirm whether any further primary material (e.g. Bárcena's lost Arte) exists. Open access but the site blocked automated download.

sources.citation: Lehmann-Nitsche, Roberto. 1930. El idioma chechehet (Pampa bonaerense). Nombres propios. Revista del Museo de La Plata 32: 277-291.
sources.note: Companion to the 1922 Het paper; analyses proper names of the Pampa language that some identify with Querandí; may repeat remarks on written accents.
sources.venue: Revista del Museo de La Plata

sources.citation: Lehmann-Nitsche, Roberto. 1922. El grupo lingüístico 'Het' de la pampa argentina. Revista del Museo de La Plata 27: 10-84.
sources.note: Not about Querandí proper (Querandí appears only in a quoted Hervás passage, p. 18 area: 'el fondo de la lengua pampa, es un dialecto querandi alterado'). On the -het language (Falkner's Chechehet/Diuihet/Taluhet) he says, p. 18 footnote, that the 18th-c. documents almost always put an accent on the i of Casuhati but 'Tratándose de un idioma del cual apenas se ha salvado una docena de palabras, no sabemos si el acento corresponde a la verdadera pronunciación de la lengua -het, o más bien, como creo, a la influencia del guaraní.' No stress rule.
sources.venue: Revista del Museo de La Plata

sources.citation: Outes, Félix F. 1897. Los querandíes. Breve contribución al estudio de la etnografía argentina. Buenos Aires: Imprenta de Martín Biedma é hijo.
sources.note: Nothing. Chapter I ('Raza - Caracteres físicos - Idioma', pp. 23-25) says philology cannot help ('La Filología.. no nos puede prestar su ayuda en este punto'), only that Querandí was distinct from Guaraní, and quotes Techo on Bárcena's lost vocabularies/artes of 'Quirandica'. Appendix 3 lists chiefs' names from the 1582 repartimiento.
sources.venue: Breve contribución al estudio de la etnografía argentina

sources.note: 40-page linguistic analysis of the 16th-17th-century Querandí personal, group and place names (Glottolog hh type 'minimal'); per the summary in Gómez et al. 2023 (Tablas 6-7, p. 9-10) this research infers a tentative consonant inventory and at least five vowels and notes graphic alternations including in accentuation ('Tancaolquepen / Tancaolquepén'); a statement on tone is not expected (corpus = written colonial spellings), at most remarks on written accent marks.
